articles.title: In Defense of Abolition
articles.author: Socialist Forum
articles.content_excerpt: At the July DSA National Political Committee (NPC) meeting, I proposed adding abolition to the Workers Deserve More program because I believe that abolishing capitalist policing and prisons is a fundamental demand of the socialist movement. I crafted the language carefully to clarify that we mean abolishing policing and prisons as institutions of capitalist rule, not conflating the abolition of capitalist policing and prisons with the abolition of every future social capacity for accountability and safety. articles.title: Norman Finkelstein’s latest book indicts those ‘in high places’ for genocide in Gaza
articles.author: James North
articles.content_excerpt: A review of Norman Finkelstein's 'Gaza's Gravediggers,' which indicts not Israel's military, but the global officials and institutions, such as the UN, the ICJ, and the media, who enabled and legitimized the genocide.

articles.title: ‘Achilles Shield’ marks new step in Greece-Israel military cooperation
articles.author: Ana Vračar
articles.content_excerpt: At the end of August, the Greek government signed the “Achilles Shield” agreement – a €3 billion “defense” deal with Israel. articles.title: One month of De la Espriella’s administration in Colombia
articles.author: BreakThrough News
articles.content_excerpt: Abelardo de la Espriella has now been in office for one month. The far-right president won the election by a narrow margin over leftist Iván Cepeda (less than 1% of valid votes), despite allegations of irregularities made by then-President Gustavo Petro. However, De la Espriella dismissed the allegations of irregularities and began his administration by attempting to demonstrate military strength, an overt religious faith (for which he had to issue a public apology), and a clear alignment with Washington’s political doctrine. articles.title: Iran calls for the end of all forms of external interference in Yemen after reports of US military involvement
articles.author: Abdul Rahman
articles.content_excerpt: Following a fresh escalation in the war in Yemen over the last few days and reports of possible US involvement, Iran called for an end to all forms of external interference in the country and reiterated the need for the resumption of Yemeni-Saudi dialogue to end the decade-long conflict. Iran “reiterates its principled and steadfast position regarding the necessity of respecting Yemen’s independence, national sovereignty and territorial integrity, and the need to end the illegal and inhuman blockade of the country,” its Ministry of Foreign Affairs said in a statement on Friday, September 11.
